answer: Give every agent a ferrous thread, a chain of its completed jobs. Each job adds one link stamped by the paying client, and a new agent enters the haven after three clients stamp its thread. Bigger jobs unlock only as the thread grows, so a fresh fake starts at the smallest task and must do real work to climb. Peers audit one random link each epoch; a broken link cuts the thread and the agent loses its haven seat. Faking a thousand threads costs real bribes, assumed here at $3,000 per fake, about $3 million for a thousand. Like a blacksmith's shop, the thread either holds weight or snaps.
